labelChirho: on behalf of, for the sake of
descriptionChirho: Benefactive sense expressing action done for someone's benefit or sake, consistently rendered by Arabic مِنْ أَجْلِ / لِأَجْلِ / عَنْ, Korean 위하여, and Swahili kwa ajili ya across all pronominal suffixes.
Spatial sense of physical movement through an opening or space, confirmed by Arabic مِنْ خِلَالِ / عَبْرَ, Korean 통하여, and Swahili kupitia; includes the interrogative 'through?' usage in Job.
Spatial sense of position or motion behind someone or something, rendered by Arabic عَلَى / وَرَاءَ / خَلْفَ, Korean 뒤에, and Swahili nyuma ya; includes 'from behind' with prepositional prefix מִן.
Sense of surrounding, encircling, or forming a protective barrier around someone, consistently marked by Arabic حَوْلَ / حَوْلِي, Korean 주위에, and Swahili kuzunguka/kulinda.

Causal sense indicating the reason or grounds for an action, distinct from the benefactive 'for the sake of'; Arabic بِسَبَبِ and Swahili kwa sababu ya confirm the causal rather than benefactive reading.
Substitutionary sense expressing replacement or exchange, clearly distinguished by Arabic بَدَلَ and Hindi के बदले, indicating something given in return rather than on someone's behalf.

Rare temporal-adverbial usage of בְּעַד in compound with other prepositions, indicating a point within or after a period of time; Arabic وَ فِي بَعدِ and Swahili na-ndani-ya confirm the temporal reading.
